headline: 23 detained from Tejgaon College mosque over suspected militant links
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police conducted a drive after receiving intelligence about a secret meeting of members from a banned militant outfit.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) detained 23 people from a mosque at Tejgaon College in the capital today following Juma prayers.
A team from the Tejgaon Police Station carried out the operation while the individuals were allegedly holding a secret meeting at the mosque.
According to a senior official of the Tejgaon Division, police acted on intelligence that members of a banned militant outfit would gather there after arriving from various parts of the city.
The official stated that police are still working to confirm whether all 23 detainees belong to the same organization.
caption:
23 people detained from a Dhaka mosque after Juma prayers. Police suspect links to a banned militant outfit.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) detained 23 people from a mosque at Tejgaon College in the capital today following Juma prayers.

A team from the Tejgaon Police Station carried out the operation while the individuals were allegedly holding a secret meeting at the mosque.

According to a senior official of the Tejgaon Division, police acted on intelligence that members of a banned militant outfit would gather there after arriving from various parts of the city.

The official stated that police are still working to confirm whether all 23 detainees belong to the same organization.

headline_marked: Rashed Khan: [[Jamaat's long march creates opportunity]] for Awami League's return
headline: Rashed Khan: Jamaat's long march creates opportunity for Awami League's return
summary: The Prime Minister's political assistant warns that the 11-party alliance's march to Rangpur could be exploited by the ousted party for sabotage.
details: Prime Minister's political assistant Rashed Khan claims that the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami is creating an opportunity for the Awami League to return to power.
During a visit to the 'Street Memory Stump' of martyr Abu Sayeed at Begum Rokeya University, Khan warned that such moves would not lead to positive results.
He alleged that the Awami League is preparing to take to the streets and carry out sabotage under the cover of the upcoming long march.
Khan also referenced a leaked audio clip of a former Cantonment police OC, who allegedly claimed the police are too weak to stop Sheikh Hasina from returning to Bangladesh.
He criticized Jamaat-e-Islami, calling them a 'reckless party' and suggesting their actions might be mirroring a 1996 political scenario where Jamaat and Awami League joined forces against the BNP.
The political assistant questioned the timing of the march, noting that the government is only seven months old and has performed commendably in its first six months.
He further challenged the 11-party alliance to walk from Dhaka to Rangpur on foot if they are truly pro-people, rather than using vehicles for 'long drives'.
The 11-party alliance is scheduled to begin their long march to Rangpur on Saturday morning, demanding an eight-point agenda.
caption:
Is a political long march paving the way for the Awami League's return? Rashed Khan warns of a dangerous pattern.

Prime Minister's political assistant Rashed Khan claims that the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami is creating an opportunity for the Awami League to return to power.

During a visit to the 'Street Memory Stump' of martyr Abu Sayeed at Begum Rokeya University, Khan warned that such moves would not lead to positive results.

He alleged that the Awami League is preparing to take to the streets and carry out sabotage under the cover of the upcoming long march.

Khan also referenced a leaked audio clip of a former Cantonment police OC, who allegedly claimed the police are too weak to stop Sheikh Hasina from returning to Bangladesh.

He criticized Jamaat-e-Islami, calling them a 'reckless party' and suggesting their actions might be mirroring a 1996 political scenario where Jamaat and Awami League joined forces against the BNP.

The political assistant questioned the timing of the march, noting that the government is only seven months old and has performed commendably in its first six months.

He further challenged the 11-party alliance to walk from Dhaka to Rangpur on foot if they are truly pro-people, rather than using vehicles for 'long drives'.

The 11-party alliance is scheduled to begin their long march to Rangpur on Saturday morning, demanding an eight-point agenda.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star
